title: Name an option by its words
statement: Never refer to an option by its letter or position in feedback, hints, explanations or instructions; name it by what it says, since the display may reorder options.
detail: A reading course's lesson-structure rules note that the player re-letters options into display order, so feedback must never say 'option C'. Its invariants for new lessons, distilled from three feedback documents on five lessons, bar meta-language anywhere a child reads, such as 'blank two', 'option A' or 'the passage states', and name a sweep that checks for it.

evidence.quote: The player RE-LETTERS options into display order — never write feedback that says "option C".
no meta-language anywhere child-facing ("blank two", "option A", "the passage states").
**Answer positions are already balanced** across A/B/C/D and explanations never name a letter, so options are safe to shuffle on render if you want.
the first option shown is always "A" regardless of its authored key
So the authored keys are identity tags, not positions — never write feedback that says "option C".
